---
title: "About"
---

I am a PhD student in the School of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University (Computational Biology Department), advised by Dr. Jose Lugo-Martinez. My research focuses on machine learning, generative and foundation models, reinforcement learning, and agentic systems, with applications to automated science and computational biology.

I develop ML methods and systems for reliable reasoning, decision-making, simulation, and scientific discovery. My projects include generative models for biological sequences, reinforcement learning for biomarker discovery, CloudBench simulation and benchmarking for programmable cloud laboratories, and agentic orchestration with fault recovery.

I value methods that are simple, strong, and reproducible, and aim to release code and minimal examples whenever possible. Before CMU, I completed my Master's at Bilkent University under Dr. A. Ercument Cicek, where I developed generative models for biological sequence optimization. My work has been published in venues including PLOS Computational Biology and Bioinformatics Advances.
